units.text: INT. ALPINE HUT - MORNING
A one-room stone refuge at the edge of a glacier.
Pine rafters, a cast-iron stove, and four bunks in a row.
Frost on the inside of the window.
Sunlight, sudden and blazing, pours through it onto a table laid with oatmeal and tin mugs.
Four climbers have just woken.
VASILIKI KOUROS, 30s, wiry and sun-darkened, stirs the pot with a wooden spoon.
TIBOR HALÁSZ, 50s, gray-bearded, gaunt, laces his boots with slow concentration.
The youngest, JACARANDA FENTON-MBEKI, 19, a rope bag over her shoulder, stands at the window, grinning at the sky.
AUGUSTINE "GUS" CALDER, 40s, their guide, sits on a bunk, back to the wall, oddly still.
The mountain outside is flawless.
Not a cloud.
Every ridge cut sharp as glass against the blue.
Look at it.
units.name: JACARANDA

units.text: I'm looking.
units.name: VASILIKI

units.text: They eat.
Spoons clink.
The stove ticks.
For a long minute it is perfect: the quiet pleasure of being alive.
Only Gus does not eat.
He is watching the window with the expression of a man reading a letter he does not want to finish.
Gus. Eat.
units.name: TIBOR

units.text: In a minute.
units.name: GUS

units.text: He rises, crosses to the window, and presses his palm to the glass.
Far away, on the western horizon, a faint white line has drawn itself across the blue, thin as a hair, and it is growing.
